title: Deploys tag the commit they shipped; pnpm release:status says what is due; deploy.sh enforces the deploy-alone rule
acceptance: After every post-deploy check passes (propagation, status smoke, security headers), scripts/deploy.sh creates an annotated tag deploy/<UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMZ>-<sha7> on the deployed commit. Its message holds the commit, the UTC deploy time, the Worker version ID, the rollback version ID and the SPA entry, and the script pushes only that ref (git push --no-follow-tags). If the script stops after the upload (a failed check, SIGTERM or SIGHUP), it prints how to tag the deploy should the owner keep it; if wrangler deploy itself fails, it says to check wrangler deployments status. A failed push keeps the local tag, prints the exact push command and exits 3; the deploy stands.

pnpm release:status (scripts/release-status.mjs: local git after git fetch origin main with deploy tags force-updated, no Cloudflare call) prints the newest deploy tag (name, commit, time), the origin/main tip and each merged commit since (PR number, title, squash SHA, whether it changes shipped code, its owner-gate classes). It ends with "deploy due" and scripts/deploy.sh <sha> steps in merge order, or "nothing to ship". It says plainly when there is no deploy tag yet and warns when the newest tag is not on origin.

A PR is deploy-alone when one of its shipped files matches scripts/owner-gate.mjs's GATES (imported, not forked). deploy.sh refuses a range from the newest deploy tag to the commit being deployed that mixes a deploy-alone PR with any other shipped change, and prints the steps, unless --allow-batch is passed. With no deploy tag yet it refuses unless --allow-batch, Separately, before the gates, it refuses when production's live Worker is not the newest tag's (a rollback, a secret change or a dashboard edit) and shows the live deployment's source; only --accept-live <the single live version at 100%> clears that, and --allow-batch does not. On the 2026-11-23 range (b9e8141 to 1eed288) the steps split #789 out.

deployment-runbook.md, start-session.md, close-session.md and AGENTS.md describe the tag, the guard, --allow-batch, --accept-live (passed only when the owner says to batch in the session, and recorded in HISTORY) and release:status.

deploy.sh --self-check covers the tag name and message, the tag push and a failed push, the guard refusal, --allow-batch, the no-tag refusal, the live version check and --accept-live, the kept-upload hint, the failed-upload note and SIGTERM. scripts/release-status.test.mjs covers the classifier, the step planner and the CLI on a fixture repo, and runs in CI and the AGENTS.md gate as pnpm release-status:test.

evidence.summary: Owner decision, Neo conductor session, recorded on iOS #113: on 2026-11-23 the owner asked for "a dependable marker to trigger deploy and TestFlight updates" and chose "Ask at every close"; on 2026-11-24 the owner answered the conductor's plan with "go". Approved: deploy.sh tags the commit it deployed (Worker version, SPA entry and rollback target in the message), pnpm release:status compares main with the newest tag and says "deploy due" or "nothing to ship", start-session reports it, and close-session asks the owner once when anything is due. Item 2 there, making the deploy-alone rule mechanical, was the conductor's recommendation; the owner approved it on 2026-11-24 (comment 7141036009).

Owner decision, Neo conductor session, 2026-11-24, recorded on iOS #113: the owner said "your \"recommendation on deploying changes alone\" are approved". That approves keeping AGENTS.md's deploy-alone rule and making it mechanical: pnpm release:status splits undeployed PRs into deploy steps with each provider/playback, auth, migration or deploy-infrastructure PR alone, and scripts/deploy.sh refuses a range that mixes such a PR with other shipped changes unless the owner says to batch in the session (--allow-batch, recorded in HISTORY). This PR stays owner-gated, so the owner still approves its merge.

Round 1124 web Lane 1 PR (owner-gated, needs-owner): the deploy tag and its push in scripts/deploy.sh, the deploy-alone guard and --allow-batch, scripts/release-status.mjs (pnpm release:status) and its test, the CI step, and the runbook, start-session, close-session and AGENTS.md text. It also files RF-245 and RF-246. Not merged by the lane; no tag was created or pushed and nothing was deployed.

bash scripts/deploy.sh --self-check passed 42 cases on the Neo (macOS bash 3.2), 17 of them RF-244's: the tag name and message; reading the Worker and rollback versions (decimal splits included; unknown when unreadable); the live version check passing a matching, unknown or untagged production; refusing a mismatch while printing the live deployment's Source line; --accept-live with the live version id passing and recorded as 'live: accepted <id> (owner, in session)'; --accept-live with a wrong or split version refused; --allow-batch alone not clearing a live mismatch; the guard refusing with no tag unless --allow-batch; a deploy-alone change alone; refusing a deploy-alone batch with the steps; --allow-batch recording the batch; the tag push sending only its own ref with push.followTags set; a failed push and a failed tag creation each exiting 3; the EXIT trap printing how to tag a kept upload; a failed wrangler deploy saying to check deployments status; and SIGTERM after the upload still running the EXIT trap (exit 143). Mutations each turned a case red, among them: --allow-batch clearing the live check, --accept-live without the equality check, no TERM trap, no failed-upload note, no Source lines, push without --no-follow-tags, exit 1 instead of 3, and a no-tag guard that passes. With GIT_DIR exported at a throwaway repo the self-check left it untouched. apps/api/src/lib/deploy-script.test.ts asserts all 17 and has a 60 s timeout.

pnpm release-status:test passed 6 of 6: the shipped-path table (.nvmrc, .npmrc and Markdown served from apps/web/public/ ship; *.fixture.* files do not), deploy-alone versus the owner-gate classes (agent rules never ship), the four 2026-11-23 PRs (#789 deploy-alone provider / playback, #790 and #792 shipped, #793 not shipped), PR-number parsing, the step planner, and the CLI on a fixture repo with a bare origin. The CLI cases: the fetch force-updating a stale local deploy tag, the newest tag by creation date (an older-dated tag with a later name is not picked), the report lines and verdicts, guard exit codes including refusal with no tag, --allow-batch, since-worker, a redeploy, an older commit that names the shipped changes it takes back (or says it takes back none), a rename out of the shipped roots, a local-only tag warning with the --no-follow-tags push command, ignored non-deploy tag names and usage errors. Each of these mutations turned it red: no --no-renames, no local-only warning, no tag-name filter, no fetch, an unforced tag refspec, sorting by name only, the old redeploy wording, a no-tag guard that passes, and all Markdown unshipped.

Rehearsed in a scratch clone of this repo with local tags only (nothing pushed): with a tag on b9e8141, release:status for the 2026-11-23 range gave two steps, scripts/deploy.sh f87c728 (#789 alone, provider / playback) then scripts/deploy.sh 1eed288 (#790, #792), and --guard 1eed288 refused with exit 1. With a tag on 1eed288, the verdict for ddc811d was "nothing to ship". On the real repo, which has no tags yet, pnpm release:status reported no deploy tag and an unknown verdict.

#796's fresh-context final review at f1915d1 (/code-review medium) found no significant findings and 17 notes. All 17 were applied on this branch, with the conductor's choices: with no deploy tag the guard refuses unless --allow-batch; deploy.sh refuses when the live Worker is not the newest tag's; the EXIT trap prints the tag command for a kept upload whose check failed; git push --no-follow-tags; self-check unsets GIT_*; the fetch force-updates deploy tags; .nvmrc, .npmrc and served Markdown ship and *.fixture.* does not; the newest tag is by creation date; the older-commit guard note; the verdict and runbook wording fixes; the decimal-percent regex with its warning; and the RF-245 and handoff fixes.

#796's follow-up review at 95444c1 found one significant finding: the runbook let the owner's rehearsal request cover --allow-batch, against AGENTS.md and the owner's 7141036009 decision. It also found five notes. All six were fixed. A rollback rehearsal now uses --accept-live <previous-version-id>, asked for with the rehearsal in one message, after confirming the newest tag's commit is <sha>. --accept-live is a separate override that clears only the live version check. The script sets DEPLOY_UPLOADING and reports a failed wrangler deploy. An older-commit deploy lists the shipped changes it takes back. TERM and HUP exit through the EXIT trap. start-session says the fetch force-updates deploy tags.

resolution: Built in #796, with all 17 notes from its final review and the follow-up review's finding and five notes applied. scripts/deploy.sh now fetches origin main with deploy tags force-updated and runs the deploy-alone guard (node scripts/release-status.mjs --guard) before it builds anything. The guard refuses a range from the newest deploy/* tag that mixes a deploy-alone change with any other shipped change, and prints the steps. It also refuses when there is no deploy tag yet; --allow-batch, on the owner's word, lets either through. Once the live version is read, it refuses when production's Worker is not the newest tag's (a rollback, a secret change or a dashboard edit), showing the live deployment's source; only --accept-live with the single live version id, on the owner's word, clears that, and the tag message records it. After the propagation loop, status smoke and security headers pass, the script tags the deployed commit deploy/<UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMZ>-<sha7>. The message carries the commit, the UTC time, the Worker version (from WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH), the rollback version (from the pre-deploy wrangler deployments status), the SPA entry, the previous tag and any allowed batch. It pushes only that ref (git push --no-follow-tags), and exits 3 with the push command if the tag cannot be created or pushed (the deploy stands). If the script stops after the upload (a failed check, SIGTERM or SIGHUP), the EXIT trap prints how to tag the deploy should the owner keep it; a failed wrangler deploy says to check deployments status. pnpm release:status reports the newest tag, the merges since with shipped and owner-gate classes, and "deploy due" with steps or "nothing to ship". Shipped means apps/api, apps/web, packages and seven root build inputs (.nvmrc and .npmrc included), minus tests and fixtures, Markdown outside apps/web/public/, and repo tools. The newest tag is the latest created. Deploy-alone means a shipped file matched by owner-gate GATES, imported unchanged. The runbook, start-session steps 5 and 9, close-session §5 and AGENTS.md describe it. Post-merge acceptance (backfilling the 1eed288 tag, the first real tagged deploy) is RF-245. The owner-gate coverage gap for scripts/release-status.mjs is RF-246.
